doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Amplifying the accordion to play bass lines like Jimmy Smith
summary: He modified his accordion with a low pass filter to get organ-like bass lines, inspired by Jimmy Smith.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So the accordion probably was a good thing to be playing because you were playing melodies and chords and bass notes, sort of like arranging as you went.

Right. Well I also learned how to play the bass lines on the accordion, and then I had my accordion amplified and I worked with someone to get a low pass filter on the amp so I can get the depth like I have an organ. So in the ‘50s I had modified the accordion to where I could play it and get a sound that was close enough to an electric organ. And that was only after I heard Jimmy Smith play. And I wanted to sound like Jimmy Smith. So I learned how to play the bass lines with my left hand. And although we had a bass player in the band, he would put his bass down and sing some of the arrangements that I wrote. So I would be playing the bass line. And it was funny to see the musicians come in to look to see where the bass was coming from.

I love that. You know I do that now but I do it on a keyboard and only rarely do I get – someone will, every once in a while say like, “Where’s the bass coming from?” Or they’ll say, “Hey you play a pretty good bass for a keyboard player.” I like it. I think that in another life I was a bass player.
